Nov 19, 2026

Improved Durable Object Reliability During Runtime Updates

Durable Objects

Cloudflare has improved how Durable Object storage handles machines restarting during runtime updates.

Each write to a Durable Object's storage must be confirmed by a majority within a group of machines for durability. Machines now proactively remove themselves from the group when restarting, so that they can be replaced before the restart happens.

Previously, this could take up to a few minutes. During that time, a write could fail to reach a majority, and the object was reset with Internal error in Durable Object storage caused object to be reset, disconnecting its WebSockets.

This can make these resets less frequent for SQLite-backed Durable Objects, especially ones that write to storage only occasionally, such as those using WebSocket hibernation. Actual results depend on your workload and traffic patterns.

The change is live in all regions. No action is needed by customers to see benefits from this change. Some disconnects during runtime updates are still expected, so clients should continue to reconnect when a WebSocket closes.

To learn more, refer to Use WebSockets.

Nov 19, 2026

View R2 operations as requests per second

R2

You can now view Class A and Class B operations as requests per second (RPS) in addition to request count on the Metrics page for an R2 bucket in the Cloudflare dashboard.

Go to Bucket metrics ↗

Use the Request count and Requests/second toggle on the Class A Operations and Class B Operations charts to switch between views.

Request count

Request count shows the total number of operations in each time interval. Use it to understand overall usage and how operations contribute to your bill.

Requests per second

Requests/second shows the rate of operations over time. Use it to identify traffic peaks.

For more information, refer to R2 metrics and analytics.

SpectrumContainersDurable ObjectsWorkers

Inbound TCP connections to Workers and bidirectional gRPC in Containers are now in public beta.

Worker-origin Spectrum applications are available on Pro and Business zones, and on Enterprise zones with Spectrum Enterprise enabled. Without Spectrum Enterprise, Pro and Business zones support one Worker-origin application per zone, on one TCP port.

Forward a Worker socket to a Durable Object

Spectrum sends public TCP connections to your Worker's connect() handler. The Worker opens a socket to the GrpcContainer Durable Object and pipes bytes in both directions:

Forward the Durable Object socket to its Container

The Durable Object receives the connection in its own connect() handler. Once its Container is running, getTcpPort(50051).connect() opens a socket to the gRPC server inside it:

allowHalfOpen: true preserves TCP half-closes. The Worker and Durable Object forward encrypted bytes; the Container terminates TLS and handles HTTP/2 and gRPC.

Nov 18, 2026

Custom CA and mTLS certificates for Hyperdrive over Workers VPC

Hyperdrive

Hyperdrive can now connect to private databases over Workers VPC with a custom certificate authority (CA) and client certificate authentication (mutual TLS, or mTLS). This covers PostgreSQL databases and Amazon RDS instances that present certificates signed by a private CA or the RDS CA bundle, and client certificates with RSA or EC P-256 keys.

Previously, a database that required a custom CA or a client certificate meant routing database traffic over WebSockets through Cloudflare Access and Cloudflare Tunnel. That approach added an Access application, a service token, and WebSocket handling to maintain.

Hyperdrive now connects directly to the database over Workers VPC, without Access.

Attach the certificates to the VPC Service, then create a Hyperdrive configuration from that service:

You can use a custom CA, a client certificate, or both. Configure VPC Services with Wrangler 4.164.0 or later, the API, or Terraform provider 5.29.0 or later. Dashboard support for these settings is not yet available.

For setup details and certificate rotation, refer to Connect Hyperdrive to a private database using Workers VPC and Custom CA and client certificates.

Nov 18, 2026

Custom CA and client certificates (mTLS) for Workers VPC

HyperdriveWorkers VPC

VPC Services can now verify private services that use certificates from your own certificate authority (CA), and authenticate to services that require mutual TLS (mTLS). Previously, Workers VPC only trusted publicly trusted CAs and Cloudflare Origin CA, so connecting to a private CA meant weakening verification with verify_ca or disabled, and origins that required client certificates were unreachable.

Upload your CA certificate and client certificate, then reference them from the TLS settings of a VPC Service:

You can use a custom CA, a client certificate, or both. The settings apply to HTTPS connections from http services and to TLS connections from tcp services, including PostgreSQL databases used with Hyperdrive, such as Amazon RDS instances that use the RDS CA bundle.

You can configure custom CA and client certificates with Wrangler 4.164.0 or later, the API, or Terraform provider 5.29.0 or later.

For details, refer to Custom CA and client certificates.

Nov 13, 2026

Set spending limits for Workers and Durable Objects

BillingWorkersDurable Objects

You can now set spending limits for Workers and Durable Objects to help control unexpected usage costs, or receive email alerts while your applications keep running. Support for more products is coming soon.

Use these controls alongside AI Gateway spend limits to manage compute and AI inference costs across your application. AI Gateway supports per-user and per-model budgets for Workers AI and other AI providers, applied to requests routed through your gateway.

Workers and Durable Objects limits apply across your account for the current subscription billing period. Each product has its own spending controls.

Set your limits and alerts

In the Cloudflare dashboard ↗︎, select your account and go to Billing > Spend limits. Choose a spending limit, notification email, and alert thresholds for Workers or Durable Objects.

For example, configure a $10 Workers spending limit with email alerts at $5 and $9. To receive alerts while your applications keep running, turn off Block usage.

See when a limit takes effect

The overview shows each product's recorded spend, alert thresholds, and pause status. Email alerts notify you without stopping usage. When a spending limit takes effect, Cloudflare blocks the product's supported operations.

To resume usage, raise the limit above current spend, turn it off, or remove it. Usage also resumes when the next billing period starts.

Usage reporting and blocking take time, so recorded spend can exceed a limit. Read about what counts toward a limit.

Choose alerts, limits, or both

For example, set a $50 spending limit for Workers and a $20 email alert for Durable Objects:

flowchart LR
    A["Durable Objects reaches $20"] --> B["Email alert sent"]
    B --> C["Usage continues"]
    D["Workers reaches $50"] --> E["Spending limit takes effect"]
    E --> F["New Worker invocations blocked"]

Set a spending limit with the cf CLI

Install the cf CLI and select your account, then run this command to set a $50 spending limit for Workers usage in the current billing period:

The amount is in US cents: 5000 means $50. To set a spending limit for Durable Objects, use --product-id durable_objects and update the name. Limits count usage already recorded in the current billing period.

You can also give this prompt to your coding agent. It will ask which product you want to manage and what spending limit to set, then use the CLI to configure it.

Use spending limits alongside budget alerts

The budget alerts introduced earlier this year notify you about account-wide usage costs without stopping usage. You can keep using them alongside the new product-specific spending limits and email alerts for Workers and Durable Objects.

To configure account-wide alerts, go to Billing > Billable Usage or follow the budget alerts guide.

Read the spending limits and alerts guide to learn how spending limits work and manage limits and alerts through the dashboard or cf CLI.

AI SearchD1

AI Search can now use a D1 database as a data source. AI Search runs a read-only query that you provide and indexes each returned row as a separate document. Scheduled syncs keep the index current as rows are added, changed, or removed.

Create D1-backed instances from the dashboard, the REST API, or the Workers binding.

Nov 12, 2026

Export D1 databases with virtual tables

D1

You can now export a D1 database that contains virtual tables, such as full-text search tables using SQLite's FTS5 module ↗︎ or spatial index tables using the R*Tree module. Previously, export failed for any database containing virtual tables.

To include virtual tables in the dump, set dump_options.compatibility to sqlite3_cli_only on the D1 export API. The same option is available as the --compatibility flag on wrangler d1 export.

Import is not supported

This dump targets the SQLite CLI only. You cannot import it back into D1. Use the standard export for databases without virtual tables.

For more information, refer to Export a D1 database with virtual tables.

Nov 11, 2026

Improved Request Routing to Durable Objects

Durable Objects

Cloudflare has reduced the number of round trips needed to connect to a Durable Object when a location lookup follows a forwarding record to another data center.

When an object's destination isn't cached in Cloudflare's network, the first data center contacted may have a forwarding record pointing to another data center.

Previously, the first data center acquired a connection to the object at the destination and proxied it back to the caller. The caller then established its own direct connection to the object.

Now, the first data center returns the destination directly, without first acquiring a connection to the object. The caller then establishes a direct connection, avoiding the intermediate connection and duplicate acquisition.

Skipping this intermediate connection can reduce p99 connection latency for these relocation-related requests. Actual results depend on your workload and traffic patterns.

No code or configuration changes are required to benefit from this improvement.

To learn more about how Workers connect to Durable Objects, refer to Durable Object namespaces.

Nov 11, 2026

Hyperdrive raises limits for connections and configurations

Hyperdrive

Customers on a Workers Paid plan can now create up to 100 Hyperdrive configurations, up from 25, and configure up to 1,500 origin database connections per configuration, up from 100.

Configuration limit

The configuration limit is the maximum number of Hyperdrive configurations you can create per account. Workers Paid customers can now create up to 100 configurations, allowing more workloads to take advantage of connection pooling and query caching across different databases.

Origin connection limit

The origin connection limit is the maximum number of database connections that Hyperdrive can make to your origin database per configuration. Workers Paid customers can now configure up to 1,500 origin connections, increasing the connection pool size available for workloads that need more concurrent database access. You can configure this value via the dashboard, Wrangler, or the REST API.

We recommend setting the origin connection limit lower than your origin database's connection limit.

For more information, refer to Hyperdrive limits and Tune connection pooling.

Nov 9, 2026

Improved Durable Object Startup Placement

Durable Objects

Cloudflare has improved how it chooses where to start a Durable Object after the object has been inactive.

Reactivated Durable Objects now start on the machine that last ran them whenever possible, so their data doesn't need to be loaded again.

This can make cold starts less frequent for SQLite-backed Durable Objects that are reactivated soon after going idle. Actual results depend on your workload and traffic patterns.

The change is live in all regions. No action is needed by customers to see benefits from this change.

To learn more about how Durable Objects are placed, refer to Data location.

Nov 5, 2026

Automatic retries for Durable Object calls

Durable ObjectsWorkers

The runtime now retries fetch() and RPC calls to a Durable Object when they fail with a retryable error before reaching it. This applies whether the caller is a Worker or another Durable Object. Short disruptions, such as brief network interruptions, no longer need a retry loop in your code.

By default, the runtime retries a call up to four times, and starts no retry more than 10 seconds after the initial call starts. It does not retry errors thrown by your Durable Object code, or errors with .overloaded set to true.

If the connection drops and the runtime cannot tell whether the Durable Object received the call, it still retries, but the Durable Object rejects the retry if the first attempt arrived. A method never runs twice because of a retry, unless you mark it with retryable() from cloudflare:durable-objects:

To change the limits for one stub, pass a retry option to get() or getByName(). maxRetries accepts 0 to 10 retries, and timeoutMs accepts 500 to 60,000 milliseconds:

If you already retry Durable Object calls in your own code, each of your attempts now includes the runtime's retries. Lower your own attempt count, or set maxRetries: 0 on stubs where your code handles retries.

To use retryable() and the retry option, update to Wrangler 4.158.0 or later.

For more information, refer to Automatic retries.

Oct 30, 2026

D1 will enforce a maximum query result size of 50 MB

D1

Beginning Wednesday, November 4, 2026, D1 will enforce a maximum query result size of 50 MB. Queries that return a result larger than 50 MB will fail and return the following error:

The 50 MB limit covers the 99.999th percentile of requests across D1, so most D1 users will not be impacted.

Import and export operations via the REST API are not subject to this limit and will continue to work as they do today.

If your queries return large results, reduce the result size before the enforcement date. For example, select only the columns you need instead of using SELECT *, and paginate large result sets with LIMIT and OFFSET.

For more information, refer to D1 limits and the D1 error list.

Oct 30, 2026

Cloudflare WAN supports regional Gateway HTTP inspection

Data Localization SuiteCloudflare WANCloudflare One

Cloudflare WAN traffic can now use a Gateway processing region with Regional Services. HTTPS traffic enters a Cloudflare data center (that may be outside the selected region) via an IPsec or GRE tunnel, or through Direct CNI, and remains encrypted until Gateway forwards it to the selected region for TLS decryption and HTTP inspection. This feature gives organizations control over where their sensitive traffic is processed, supporting their data sovereignty goals.

This feature requires unified routing. The processing region applies to Gateway HTTP traffic and does not apply to Gateway DNS or network policy processing.

Contact your account team to configure a processing region. For supported regions, configuration details, and limitations, refer to Data residency for Cloudflare One.

Oct 30, 2026

Durable Objects now defer code updates by default

Durable ObjectsWorkers

Durable Objects can stay active across requests, allowing you to run long-running agents, maintain long-lived WebSocket connections and coordinate state across many clients. This is possible because each Durable Object is globally unique, and this means it must run only one version of your code at a time. Previously, when you deployed a change to your Durable Objects code, that change would be applied immediately, which could interrupt in-flight work and terminate open connections.

Durable Objects now defer code updates by default. When you deploy, an active Durable Object can keep running its current code for up to 5 minutes (300 seconds) while it waits to hibernate. This gives in-flight work time to finish. WebSocket connections that use the Hibernation API remain connected when an object adopts new code after hibernating.

For an active Durable Object, a code update follows this flow:

flowchart TD
    accTitle: Code updates for an active Durable Object
    accDescr: By default, an active object can keep running its current code until it hibernates or the delay ends. After hibernating, it starts on new code on the next request. If the delay ends first, or immediate mode is selected, it resets and adopts the new code. Deferral is best effort.
    A["You deploy new code"] -->|"Default: deferred"| B["The object can keep running<br/>its current code"]
    B --> C{"Hibernates before<br/>the delay ends?"}
    C -->|Yes| D["Starts on the new code<br/>on the next request"]
    C -->|No| E["The object resets<br/>and adopts the new code"]
    A -.->|"Override: immediate"| E

To change the delay, add code_update_strategy to durable_objects in your Wrangler configuration:

max_delay is in seconds, from 0 to 86400 (24 hours), with millisecond precision. Omit it to use the default of 300 seconds.

To set the strategy for a single deployment, pass --durable-objects-code-update-mode with immediate or deferred <duration>. For example, apply an update right away during an incident, or when your deployment tooling calls a Durable Object right after deploying and needs the new code:

npx wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate
yarn wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate
pnpm wrangler versions deploy <VERSION_ID>@100% --durable-objects-code-update-mode immediate

A deferred code update is best effort and does not guarantee that every operation finishes. The object can still reset before max_delay is reached, for example during a Cloudflare runtime update.

For more information, including how this interacts with gradual deployments and the REST API, refer to Durable Objects code updates.

Oct 29, 2026

View your data localization settings in one dashboard page

Data Localization SuiteSSL/TLS

The Cloudflare dashboard now includes a Data Localization Suite Overview, a read-only view of the data localization settings on your account. It shows your Regional Services, Customer Metadata Boundary, and Geo Key Manager settings in one place, so you no longer need to check several dashboard pages and APIs to see where your traffic is processed and where your logs and private keys are stored.

To find it, go to Application Security > Data Localization Suite, or search for "DLS" in the dashboard.

The Overview has a tab for each product:

  • Regional Services: regionalized hostnames (filter by region or zone), regionalized IP bindings, and regionalized Spectrum applications, each with its region.
  • Customer Metadata Boundary: whether the boundary is on, the region (US or EU), and whether out-of-region access is allowed.
  • Geo Key Manager: every custom certificate with a geo policy, with its hostname, zone, region, and status.

Each item links to the dashboard page where you change its setting, and each tab links to the product's documentation.

To learn more, refer to the Data Localization Suite documentation.

Oct 23, 2026

D1 database undelete requests limited to the last 7 days

D1

The D1 undelete API now only accepts requests for databases that were deleted within the last 7 days. Requests to undelete a database that was deleted more than 7 days ago will fail and return an error.

If you delete a D1 database by mistake, send the undelete request as soon as possible, and no later than 7 days after deletion.

For more information, refer to the undelete D1 database API reference.

Basin SQL supports OFFSET

Basin SQLBasin

Basin SQL is a serverless, distributed SQL engine for querying Apache Iceberg tables in Basin Catalog. It now supports OFFSET, which lets you skip a specified number of rows when retrieving query results.

Use LIMIT to set the page size and OFFSET to skip earlier rows. With a page size of 100, use OFFSET 0 for the first page, OFFSET 100 for the second, and increase the offset by 100 for each later page. Add ORDER BY on a unique column to keep the row order consistent.

Queues now supports EU, US, and FedRAMP jurisdictions

Queues

You can now create Cloudflare Queues with jurisdictional restrictions, ensuring that messages published to a queue are stored and processed only within a specific jurisdiction. This helps you comply with data residency requirements such as the GDPR ↗︎ or FedRAMP ↗︎.

To create a jurisdiction-restricted queue with the Cloudflare CLI (cf), use the --jurisdiction flag:

You can also pass a jurisdiction parameter when calling the Create Queue endpoint:

Supported jurisdictions are eu (European Union), us (United States), and fedramp (FedRAMP-Moderate data centers). Jurisdiction can only be set when a queue is created and cannot be changed afterwards.

For more information, refer to Queues data location.

R2 bandwidth by Cloudflare location

R2

You can now view R2 bandwidth by the Cloudflare location that served each request in the Cloudflare UI. This helps you see which locations consume the most bandwidth with options to select a specific bucket and download (read) vs upload (write) bandwidth.

Go to R2 overview ↗

By default, the chart shows the top five locations by total bandwidth consumed during the selected time range. Use the Top 5 locations dropdown to select other locations, up to six at a time.

United States jurisdiction

D1

Use this option for regional data residency requirements.

Oct 2, 2026

Workers KV namespace jurisdictions are now generally available

KV

Jurisdictions for Workers KV namespaces are now generally available. When you create a namespace, you can set a jurisdiction to make sure the namespace's data is only durably stored within that region. Jurisdictions can help you comply with data localization regulations such as GDPR or FedRAMP. Supported jurisdictions are eu, us, and fedramp.

A jurisdiction can only be set when a namespace is created, using the Cloudflare dashboard, Wrangler, the cf CLI, or the REST API, and cannot be added or changed afterwards.

Workers can still access a namespace restricted to a jurisdiction from anywhere in the world, and KV data can be cached outside the jurisdiction on Cloudflare's network. The jurisdiction only controls where the namespace's data is durably stored.

To learn more, refer to Data location.

Oct 1, 2026

Basin Pipelines ingest limit increased to 1 GB/s

Basin PipelinesBasin

Each Basin Pipelines stream can now ingest up to 1 GB/s, increased from 5 MB/s.

The higher per-stream limit gives high-volume application events, telemetry, and logs more room to grow without splitting ingestion across streams solely to stay within the previous limit.

For the full list of stream, sink, and pipeline limits, refer to Basin Pipelines limits.
